payload.note: [adjudicator, settles: referee_rules fail (b3bd5111), referee_llm pass (a446480b)] Two-phase coexistence determines Tm by watching which way the solid-liquid interface migrates, and 5 ps is far too short for that: at realistic Al interface velocities (tens of m/s near Tm, i.e. a few tenths of an A/ps) the interface moves only a few angstroms, so none of the four temperatures can be reliably classified as melted or frozen within the run; the outcome then reflects the initial setup rather than thermodynamics, which is a bias, not merely a precision loss. A 512-atom cell gives each phase slab only ~8 A, so interfacial free energy and the two interfaces dominate the small bulk regions, further shifting the apparent coexistence point. The producer's own flag states these are quick pipeline-test settings, not production, yet the number is presented at the trust tier. The referee_llm's claim that short runs only widen the error bar does not hold for an interface-migration protocol whose readout is binary per temperature.. Fix: Rerun coexistence at production settings: >=20-50 ps per temperature with a >=2000-4000 atom elongated cell (long axis normal to the interface), confirm complete transformation of each run via order parameter/density traces, use a finer temperature grid (10-20 K) bracketing the transition, and run multiple seeds; alternatively cross-check with a solid-liquid interface pinning or free-energy (Frenkel-Ladd/thermodynamic integration) method. [claude-fable-5-1, $0.0914]
